_doc: WHY. A VM twin is only worth trusting if it catches what the browser copy
catches. Equal test COUNTS prove nothing — tools/ci/twinned-specs.mjs's own
check is trivially satisfied by an adapted spec, because the twin IS the
spec. So each row breaks one real mechanism and names WHICH tests must go
red. The asymmetry is the whole point: a mutant that reddens every test
proves only that the suite runs.
`find` is pinned to a CONSTANT, never a line number, so a refactor moves it
without silently voiding the mutant; tests/unit/twin-fidelity.test.mjs fails
the moment a `find` string stops existing.
`mutants` GATE. `openQuestions` do not: they are mutants that SHOULD bite and
measurably do not, kept here because deleting them would delete the evidence.

mutants.why: Kills the steer-scaled wall scrub, so leaning gently on the barrier costs the same as burying the wheel in it — the flat stop the scrub test was written against.

mutants.find: const bufferAt = (ns) => Math.max(threshold(bufferNs, bufferDefault, ns), consoleAt(ns));
mutants.why: Drops the max() that keeps the ring at or above the console level, so logLevel("scenery:debug") prints debug lines the very next __apex.logs() cannot show — the empty-ring trap log.js records.

mutants.find: const lat = (wx - bestCx) * r0 + (wz - bestCz) * r2;
mutants.replace: const lat = -((wx - bestCx) * r0 + (wz - bestCz) * r2);
mutants.why: Flips the sign of the lateral offset Tracks.project() recovers, so a car right of the centreline projects as left — the +right convention every agent-view and debris consumer relies on silently inverts.

mutants.find: return { level: 0, sector: -1, frac: 0, total: 0, sectors: [0, 0, 0], sinceT: 0, cause: "", phase: "" };
mutants.replace: return { level: 0, sector: -1, frac: 0, total: 0, sectors: [0, 0], sinceT: 0, cause: "", phase: "" };
mutants.why: The blank caution state carries two sectors instead of three, so a machine reading the per-sector picture would fly green through the third sector — the per-sector contract the boot test pins.
Renames the level-0 flag label, so caution() reports something other than GREEN while level is 0 — the label the HUD chips and agent consumers key on drifts from the state machine.
Lifts the rear-wing sponsor band 50 mm off the flap skin, the ~90 mm float the band shipped with when it was authored off the design chord instead of the hung flap pose.
Moves the exitsOntoStraight threshold away from the 120 m the flag is documented as deriving from, so the boolean disagrees with the straightAfterM metric an agent reads beside it.
Widens the lane tolerance until the racing line counts as the pit box, so a car that halts mid-road is serviced — the quiet reversal inLaneLat's floor comment warns a later circuit could cause.

Flattens the past-life cliff to the in-life slope, so a set five laps over its life costs the same per lap as a fresh one — the strategy pressure the model exists to create disappears while every in-life number stays exactly right.

Makes traction lose the whole lateral drop instead of a share of it, so a worn set reads as an engine failure rather than a handling change — the asymmetry the degradation model is built around goes flat.

Raises the corner-detection threshold tenfold (R < 17 m instead of R < 170 m), so every real corner reads as a flat-out kink: the racing line, its apexes and the attack zones the AI and the agent view derive from it all vanish while a straight still reports no line.

openQuestions.test: lap distance stays continuous driving wide through Monaco
openQuestions.finding: That test's comment calls it 'a guard that the projection stays continuous (and that future changes don't reintroduce a teleport)'. It is not. THREE separate mutations of project() leave it green: CONT = 0 (the arc-length penalty removed), CONT inverted (cost -= ..., which actively REWARDS snapping far from the last arc), and W = track.n (the +/-16-node locality window opened to a global nearest-point search, the pre-hint behaviour that caused the original teleports).

W = track.n.browser: not measured — two browser columns already agreed

openQuestions.sowhat: The test costs ~110 s of browser per run and guards less than it claims. Before it can gate anything, someone has to find driving that MAKES the projection ambiguous (roadFollow 0.7 may hold the car too near the line for a hairpin to be ambiguous at all) — and until then it should not be cited as projection coverage. Recorded rather than quietly deleted: docs/notes/DEFECT-LEDGER.md, 2026-09-16.

openQuestions.test: can drive safely via emulated tilt input
openQuestions.finding: The tilt test's floor (distPct > 30, maxWall < 1, finite) cannot see a dead tilt pipeline. Two mutations of the tilt map leave it green: MAX_TILT = 36000 (a no-op — js/input/steer-tuning.js re-applies MAX_TILT through the 8..60-clamped setTiltSensitivity at boot) and tiltTarget()'s gain scaled by 1e-3 (the steer command never moves: jitter 0).

tiltTarget gain * 1e-3.twin: 1/1 green (175 s); with the map dead the lap reports jitter 0, distPct 44.1, maxWall 0, finite true — the autopilot's wedge recovery keeps the throttle on and the car crawls 44 % of Monza in 150 s with 4378 of 9000 frames off-road (7.68 m over the edge); ROAD_FOLLOW defaults to 0, so no assist masks it

openQuestions.sowhat: autopilot.spec.js is portable and 3/3 green under the adapter (168 s) but stays on the browser gate: without a mutant that bites, listing it as ADAPTED would be the vacuous count check the fidelity gate exists to refuse. Before it can move, the test needs a floor a dead tilt map fails — e.g. steer-command variance, or off-road frames bounded — measured in a browser first. Recorded 2026-09-22.
